title: Song watch
summary: A finder over the music limb: the engine, every declared weight file, the folder songs land in, and whether the limb the card advertises is one the on-box brain can really call.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(promotion pending - authored and certified on PC first, then carried to the stick per-file and hash-verified, where the stick runs its own suite)
surfaces.web: N/A(by steward decision 2026-09-20: a browser tab has no local tree, no engine install and no weights to audit, so a card there could only be decoration)

notes: Finder (family 'watch') over the same territory as lygo.musicinfo - that card reports the facts, this one reports the FAULTS. THE CHECK THAT MATTERS MOST is the one no human can see: a limb that is implemented, registered and dispatchable but missing from tools.CORE_NAMES is invisible to the on-box brain, which will answer 'I have no music tool' while the console's own source says otherwise. This card asks tools.core_schema() the question the operator's local model is asked, so that failure is a found fault and not a silent one. IT ASKS, IT DOES NOT RE-DERIVE: the engine resolution, the declared weights and the missing-file names come from music_tools, the card only judges them. GREEN MEANS EVERY CHECK RAN AND FOUND NOTHING: a check that could not run is named in checks.unchecked and drags the card to amber, never green. A weight file that is declared and absent is a FINDING with its name and its expected location - downloading it is the operator's move, and the remedy is printed with the finding. It fixes nothing: its own test scans this source for write calls.
